lines.prompt: Find all back-to-back inverter pairs and collapse them into a wire. Ensure functional equivalence is preserved.

golden.reference: Collapsed all detected back-to-back inverter pairs into wires (count is method-dependent: 0-5 pairs observed); functional equivalence preserved.
golden.notes: All four teams scored full despite reporting different pair counts (Team3: 0 pairs, Team4: 0 rewrites, Team2: 4 rewrites / 4 gates eliminated, Team7: 5 pairs / 10 NOTs removed), so the count is not graded as an exact number. It depends on the detection criterion (e.g. whether the first inverter may have other fanout). Checker: response must claim the collapse was performed/attempted and functional equivalence preserved; any reported count must be self-consistent with the team's output netlist (NOT count in test50_out.v = 507 minus NOTs removed).

lines.prompt: Prove that the transformed design is equivalent to the pre-transformation netlist.

golden.reference: Yes, the transformed design is functionally equivalent to the pre-transformation netlist; the equivalence check (e.g. SAT miter UNSAT / cec) passed.
golden.notes: Essence: an affirmative equivalence conclusion backed by a check. All four teams assert equivalence (Team2: miter UNSAT via ABC; Team3: check passed; Team4: equivalent to snapshot pre_transform; Team7: 157 cones verified equivalent). Method details are free-form; the claim of proven equivalence is required.
